title: Anthropic completes biggest IPO ever, raises over $81 billion
dek: Anthropic’s stock will begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT after the offering topped SpaceX as the largest on record.
body:
Anthropic’s initial public offering raised more than $81 billion, making it the largest IPO on record and surpassing SpaceX, according to CNBC. Techzine Global reports the offering totaled $81.3 billion. Anthropic stock is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT on Thursday.

## Why it matters

This is a landmark capital event for the AI sector: the size of the raise injects a large pool of public capital into one of the leading AI firms and sets a new benchmark for future offerings. The scale of the deal has immediate implications for investors, corporate competitors, and the allocation of capital within the AI industry. The transaction also draws regulatory and market attention because of its unprecedented size relative to prior technology IPOs.

## The details

- Anthropic’s IPO raised over $81 billion, described as the largest offering on record by CNBC. Techzine Global reports the total as $81.3 billion.
- The offering surpasses SpaceX’s previous record for largest IPO, according to CNBC.
- Anthropic’s shares will begin trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on Thursday, according to CNBC.
- Specifics not reported in the cited coverage include the IPO price per share, Anthropic’s implied market valuation after the offering, the list of underwriters, the allocation of shares between insiders and new public investors, and any lockup terms for existing shareholders.

## What to watch

Trading begins on Thursday, which will reveal market demand through the initial public market price action. Watch for published details that CNBC and other outlets have not reported yet: the IPO price per share, Anthropic’s market capitalization implied by that price, and disclosures about share allocation and any lockup agreements. These remaining figures will determine how the headline figure translates into control, capital available for operations and growth, and immediate returns for early investors and employees.

Source: reporting by CNBC.
author: Kelvane Club Desk
